key_insight: This survey connects video understanding, video generation, and video world models through one idea: a video is a partial, lossy view of a changing world. Modeling that underlying world offers a common framework for studying these capabilities.
problem_solved: Video foundation models and world models often have different objectives and are studied separately. The survey addresses the need for a unified perspective on how video observations relate to underlying world dynamics.
method: Use world modeling as a unifying lens for reviewing video foundation models and video world models.
Treat observed video as a partial, lossy, temporally ordered projection of a latent, evolving world.
Examine video understanding and generation in terms of their relationship to observations and world dynamics.
impact: This perspective can help AI/ML practitioners distinguish modeling visible video patterns from modeling underlying world dynamics. It provides a conceptual bridge between video understanding and generation, rather than introducing a new model.
visual_elements: A changing world projected through a camera into a video timeline, with hidden information shaded out.
A three-part diagram linking video understanding, video generation, and world modeling.
An iceberg illustration contrasting visible frames with latent world state and dynamics.
A sequence of frames showing how limited observations reveal only part of an evolving scene.
paper_title: Reading, Writing, Sharing, and Interacting with the World through Video
paper_authors: Shengqiong Wu, Meng Luo, Bobo Li, Ziwei Liu, Shuicheng Yan
